title: The supported Koszul summand forces invertibility of the open unit
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with derived localizations for module sheaves and open restrictions [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $T\subseteq X$ be closed with quasi-compact complement. Let $U$ be a quasi-compact open and $V$ an affine open with $X=U\cup V$. Let $R$ be any right adjoint of the derived restriction $L$ to the localized module site on $U$, with a specified adjunction. Let $Q$ be a perfect quasi-coherent object supported on $T$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. There exists a perfect quasi-coherent $E$ supported on $T$ with $Q$ a retract of $E$, such that for every quasi-coherent $K$ supported on $T$, vanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}(E[n],K)$ for all integers $n$ implies that the adjunction unit $K\to R L K$ is invertible. Support means zero cohomology stalks outside $T$. This statement asserts only invertibility of the unit, without a smaller-cover hypothesis or a global zero-detection conclusion.

proof.text: Apply the supported Koszul relative detector on U,V to obtain A, perfect and supported on T, whose restriction to U is zero, and which detects supported objects zero on U.

Form E = Q plus A in the ambient derived category. Homology preserves binary biproducts, and binary sums of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent. Apply two out of three to the split distinguished triangle Q to E to A to obtain perfectness. Applying the additive stalk-homology functor to the biproduct total identity proves support. Inclusions and projections give retracts of Q and A.
Complete the specified unit K to R(L(K)) to a distinguished triangle with cone C. The supported open-unit cone theorem supplies quasi-coherence and support on T of C, and L(C)=0.

Shift the retract of A from E to transfer all Hom vanishing to A. Since L(A)=0 and L commutes with shifts, adjunction gives Hom(A[n],R(L(K)))=0. Integer shift equivalence gives Hom(A[n],K[1])=0 from Hom(A[n-1],K)=0. The exact coyoneda sequence of the unit triangle gives Hom(A[n],C)=0. Apply the relative detector to C, obtaining C=0. The Mathlib distinguished-triangle zero-cone criterion then gives IsIso of the original unit.

lean.statement: theorem exists_supported_koszul_unit_summand (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) (U : X.Opens) (V : X.affineOpens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (hcover : U ⊔ (V : X.Opens) = ⊤) (R : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ⥤ schemeDerivedCategory X) (adj : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ R) (Q : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X) (hQ : Scheme.IsPerfect X Q.obj) (hQT : (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T → Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj Q.obj).val.presheaf x)))) : ∃ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, Scheme.IsPerfect X E.obj ∧ (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T → Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E.obj).val.presheaf x))) ∧ Nonempty (Retract Q.obj E.obj) ∧ ∀ K : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X, (∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T → Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K.obj).val.presheaf x))) → (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (E.obj⟦n⟧ ⟶ K.obj)) → IsIso (adj.unit.app K.obj)
